In [[algebraic geometry]], '''Procesi bundles''' are [[vector bundle]]s of rank <math>n!</math> on certain [[symplectic resolution]]s of quotient singularities, particularly on the [[Hilbert scheme]] of <math>n</math> points in the [[complex plane]].<ref name="losev2014"/> They play a fundamental role in [[geometric]] [[representation theory]] and were crucial in [[Mark Haiman]]'s proof of the [[n! theorem]] and [[Macdonald positivity conjecture]], and were named after [[Italians|Italian]] [[mathematician]] [[Claudio Procesi]].
== Definition ==
Let <math>H_n = \text{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)</math> denote the [[Hilbert scheme]] of n points in the complex plane <math>\mathbb{C}^2</math>, which provides a [[resolution of singularities]] of the [[quotient group|quotient]] <math>(\mathbb{C}^2)^n/S_n</math>, where <math>S_n</math> is the [[symmetric group]] of degree <math>n</math>. A Procesi bundle <math>\mathcal{P}</math> on <math>H_n</math> is a <math>\mathbb{C}^{\times}</math>-equivariant vector bundle of rank <math>n!</math> together with an [[isomorphism]] <math>\text{End}(\mathcal{P}) \cong \mathbb{C}[x,y]\#S_n</math> (where <math>\mathbb{C}[x,y]\#S_n</math> is the [[Group Hopf algebra#Hopf_module_algebras_and_the_Hopf_smash_product|smash product algebra]]) of <math>\mathbb{C}[V]^{S_n}</math>-algebras, such that <math>\text{Ext}^i(\mathcal{P},\mathcal{P}) = 0</math> for all <math>i > 0</math>. The isomorphism ensures that each [[fiber (mathematics)|fiber]] of <math>\mathcal{P}</math> is naturally the [[regular representation]] of <math>S_n</math>.<ref name="losev2014" />

More generally, for a [[finite group|finite subgroup]] <math>\Gamma \subset \text{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})</math> and its [[wreath product]] <math>\Gamma_n = S_n \ltimes \Gamma^n</math>, Procesi bundles can be defined on symplectic resolutions of <math>\mathbb{C}^{2n}/\Gamma_n</math>.<ref name="losev2014"/>

== Properties ==
Procesi bundles provide a derived [[McKay graph|McKay equivalence]] between the derived [[category (mathematics)|category]] of [[coherent sheaves]] on <math>H_n</math> and the derived category of <math>S_n</math>-equivariant [[module (mathematics)|modules]] over <math>\mathbb{C}[x,y]</math>. For one distinguished Procesi bundle <math>\mathcal{P}</math>, the <math>\Gamma_{n-1}</math>-invariants <math>\mathcal{P}^{S_{n-1}}</math> coincide with the [[tautological bundle]] on <math>H_n</math>. On any symplectic resolution of <math>\mathbb{C}^{2n}/\Gamma_n</math>, there are exactly two normalized (meaning <math>\mathcal{P}^{S_n} \cong \mathcal{O}</math>) Procesi bundles which are [[duality (mathematics)|dual]] to each other.<ref name="losev2019"/>
== History and constructions ==
The first construction of a Procesi bundle was given by [[Americans|American]] mathematician [[Mark Haiman]] in his proof of the [[n! theorem]], using intricate combinatorial methods.<ref name="haiman2001">{{cite journal|last=Haiman|first=Mark|title=Hilbert schemes, polygraphs and the Macdonald positivity conjecture|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|volume=14|issue=4|year=2001|pages=941–1006|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-01-00373-3 }}</ref> Alternative constructions were later developed by [[Roman Bezrukavnikov]] and Dmitry Kaledin using [[Quantization (signal processing)|quantization]] in [[positive characteristic]],<ref name="BK">{{cite journal|last1=Bezrukavnikov|first1=Roman|last2=Kaledin|first2=Dmitry|title=McKay equivalence for symplectic quotient singularities|journal=Proceedings of the Steklov Institute of Mathematics|volume=246|year=2004|pages=13–33}}</ref> and by [[Victor Ginzburg]] using [[D-module|''D''-module]]s and the [[Hotta-Kashiwara construction]].<ref name="ginzburg">{{cite journal|last=Ginzburg|first=Victor|title=Isospectral commuting variety, the Harish-Chandra D-module, and principal nilpotent pairs|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|volume=161|issue=11|year=2012|pages=2023–2111|doi=10.1215/00127094-1699392 |arxiv=1108.5367 }}</ref>

Belarusian-American mathematician [[Ivan Losev (mathematician)|Ivan Losev]] provided significant further developments in the theory of Procesi bundles, including a complete classification of Procesi bundles on [[Momentum map|Hamiltonian reductions]],<ref name="losev2014">{{cite journal|last=Losev|first=Ivan|title=On Procesi bundles|journal=Mathematische Annalen|volume=359|issue=3|year=2014|pages=729–744|doi=10.1007/s00208-014-1017-7 }}</ref> and an [[induction (mathematics)|inductive]] construction showing how Procesi bundles relate to nested [[Hilbert scheme]]s.<ref name="losev2019">{{cite arXiv |last=Losev|first=Ivan|title=On inductive construction of Procesi bundles |date=2019 |class=math.AG |eprint=1901.05862 }}</ref> His work established that there are exactly two normalized Procesi bundles on any given symplectic resolution obtained by Hamiltonian reduction.

As a result of their use in the proof of the [[n! theorem]], Procesi bundles have also found important applications in the proof of the [[Macdonald positivity conjecture]],<ref name="haiman2001" /> the study of [[rational variety|rational]] [[Double affine Hecke algebra|Cherednik algebras]] and their representations, and understanding derived equivalences for symplectic quotient singularities.<ref name="BK" /><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gordon|first1=Iain|title=Macdonald positivity via the Harish-Chandra D-module|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=187|year=2012|issue=3 |pages=637–643|doi=10.1007/s00222-011-0339-2 |bibcode=2012InMat.187..637G |url=https://www.pure.ed.ac.uk/ws/files/8251650/MACDONALD_POSITIVITY_VIA_THE_HARISH_CHANDRA_D_MODULE.pdf }}</ref>
